title: What's the deal with Bond, James Bond?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the James Bond franchise: Ian Fleming's background and wartime service, the novels and their out-of-order film adaptations, the evolution of the Bond character (Scottish father backstory, double-O status, Q, M, Moneypenny), the actors who played Bond (Barry Nelson on TV's Climax, Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan, Daniel Craig), villains and Bond girls, theme songs, box office, and the "Bond as multiple men" fan theory. The episode closes with a listener mail about the samurai Miyamoto Musashi and wooden bokken swords.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with light banter about Bond as a blunt instrument of the crown and his gadget-laden reputation.

segments.title: Ian Fleming's wartime service
segments.summary: Fleming was a journalist and stockbroker who served in the Royal Navy in WWII, including a Washington intelligence assignment. William Stevenson (Intrepid) is named as a real-life inspiration, and Roald Dahl was in the same spy ring.

segments.title: Fleming's novels and Jamaica
segments.summary: Fleming wrote the Bond novels at his Jamaica home, named GoldenEye. Hosts debate whether he wrote thirteen or fourteen books, settling on twelve novels plus short story collections. The films were not made in publication order; Dr. No was the first film but the sixth novel. Thunderball litigation delayed its film adaptation.

segments.title: Bond's name and Scottish backstory
segments.summary: Fleming reportedly chose the name James Bond for its blandness. Fleming gave Bond a Scottish father and Swiss mother after being impressed by Sean Connery. Bond's birthdate varies across accounts.

segments.title: Bond's MI6 career and double-O status
segments.summary: Bond served in WWII, rose to commander, then joined MI6. His first two assignments were assassinations, earning double-O status, and the 007 designation.

segments.title: Bond's traits and Walther PPK
segments.summary: Bond is described as a sharp dresser who likes fast cars, martinis and women, and as a martial artist who carried the Walther PPK. The hosts discuss shaken versus stirred martinis and a GoldenEye video game.

segments.title: Bond villains
segments.summary: Discussion of villains including Dr. No, Goldfinger, Oddjob, Jaws, Blofeld and SPECTRE, Max Zorin, and Alec Trevelyan, with comparisons of recent villains to classic ones.

segments.title: M, Q, Moneypenny and allies
segments.summary: The hosts describe Bond's MI6 colleagues: M, the head of MI6 played by Judi Dench; Q, head of the Q branch who supplies gadgets; R, the successor to Q; Felix Leiter, Jack Wade; and Moneypenny, M's assistant.

segments.title: Bond on television and Climax
segments.summary: Bond first appeared on screen in a CBS TV adaptation called Climax, with Barry Nelson as an American Bond. Other Bond actors are listed by nationality. George Lazenby's career faded after one film. Casino Royale parodies and Never Say Never Again are mentioned.

segments.title: Bond actors and Never Say Never Again
segments.summary: Connery returned in the unofficial Never Say Never Again after pledging never to play Bond again. Dalton, Brosnan and Craig's tenures are compared, and Roger Moore's seven films are defended. Sam Neill is mentioned as a considered candidate.

segments.title: Bond fan theory of multiple men
segments.summary: A fan theory holds that each actor played a different man using the James Bond name, which the hosts say explains personality changes, though holes exist. Recommended sites are mentioned.

segments.title: Albert Broccoli and MGM
segments.summary: Albert R. Broccoli's family reportedly helped develop broccoli, and he left the family farm for Hollywood. The hosts note MGM's financial troubles delaying Bond 23.

segments.title: Bond girls and theme songs
segments.summary: Bond girls such as Ursula Andress, Honey Rider, Pussy Galore, Solitaire, Holly Goodhead, and Stacey Sutton are discussed alongside Bond theme songs by Shirley Bassey, Carly Simon, Nancy Sinatra, Tom Jones, Garbage, Sheryl Crow, Madonna, and Jack White with Alicia Keys.

segments.title: Title sequences and box office
segments.summary: Opening title sequences and cold openings are discussed. The hosts compare highest-grossing Bond films, with Casino Royale's worldwide gross and the adjusted grosses of Thunderball and Goldfinger.

segments.title: Cars and Inspector Gadget
segments.summary: The hosts name Bond's favorite cars, including the Aston Martin, Lotus and Alfa Romeo, and joke that Inspector Gadget resembles Bond.

segments.title: Listener mail: samurai and Miyamoto Musashi
segments.summary: A listener from Thomas writes about Miyamoto Musashi, author of The Book of Five Rings, and about wooden bokken swords used in battle.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh asks for listener information about Bond and gives the show's mail address before the sponsor message closes the episode.
